Walkthrough

The webhook service now builds a GitHub review publisher and posts advisory `COMMENT` reviews. It uses installation tokens with explicitly allowed write permissions, checks local and GitHub records for duplicate posts, and handles posting failures, retries, and superseded jobs. **Changes: Webhook review publishing** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Posting permissions and token deadlines**
`atlas_reviewer/github_auth.py`, `atlas_reviewer/tests/test_github_auth.py`, `atlas_reviewer/tests/test_service_post.py`|Installation tokens can request specifically allowed write permissions. Mint requests use a per-thread timeout override, and tests cover permission validation and timeout behavior.| |**COMMENT rendering and idempotent posting**
`atlas_reviewer/service_post.py`, `atlas_reviewer/tests/test_service_post.py`|The poster renders bounded, scrubbed COMMENT bodies, checks local and GitHub review records for matching markers, and classifies HTTP responses and retry waits. Tests cover posting, duplicate detection, rate limits, and worker shutdown.| |**Publisher setup and service settlement**
`atlas_reviewer/service.py`, `atlas_reviewer/README.md`, `atlas_reviewer/tests/test_service_post.py`, `atlas_reviewer/tests/test_service_receive.py`, `docs/open-questions.md`|The service builds the publisher from environment settings, redacts configured credentials, and settles posting failures. Documentation describes the service and its posting rules; tests cover publisher startup and credential scrubbing.| |**Pending-post and supersede lifecycle**
`atlas_reviewer/service_queue.py`, `atlas_reviewer/tests/test_service_receive.py`|Superseded pending jobs are returned for cleanup. Paused posting jobs retain the superseded state when applicable, and save failures restore the prior posting state and cancellation flag.| **Estimated code review effort:** 4 (Complex) | ~45 minutes **Change:** Feature ### Sequence Diagram(s) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant ServiceWorker participant ReviewPoster participant PostLedger participant AppInstallationTokens participant GitHubAPI ServiceWorker->>ReviewPoster: Post completed review ReviewPoster->>PostLedger: Check repository, pull request, and commit key ReviewPoster->>GitHubAPI: Search reviews for a matching marker ReviewPoster->>AppInstallationTokens: Mint installation token AppInstallationTokens->>GitHubAPI: Request token with allowed permissions ReviewPoster->>GitHubAPI: Create COMMENT review if no match exists and the head is current ReviewPoster->>PostLedger: Record accepted review ID ``` **Suggested reviewers:** `cursoragent`
Merge Risk: Moderate · previous review 10d1c

With the documented entry point, the check that blocks posting for a head that has already moved never runs, so a stale commit can receive a review that cannot be withdrawn. A shutdown while the service lists existing reviews can also discard a finished review for good. Fix both before merging.

The changeset adds a COMMENT-only posting path (service_post.py with comment_only, RefusedR… | | Linked Issues check | ![Passed](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/pre-merge-checks-passed.svg) | Check skipped because no linked issues were found for this pull request. | | Out of Scope Changes check | ![Passed](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/pre-merge-checks-passed.svg) | Check skipped because no linked issues were found for this pull request. |
Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the primary change: webhook reviews are posted as a single COMMENT review and never APPROVE. The changeset adds a COMMENT-only posting path (service_post.py with comment_only, RefusedReviewEvent, and comment_payload), tests for event refusal, and decision D46 in the docs. The title is specific and matches the objectives in PR `#640`.

# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues
